body:
## 做咗咩

加一個 **Windows 適配層** 落 `.claude/skills/docgen/`,令上游 `document-skills` plugin(xlsx / docx / pptx / pdf)喺呢部機真係跑得起。

上游 plugin 本身寫得好好,但**佢啲執行命令假設 Linux 沙箱**。喺 Windows 有五個會壞,其中三個係**靜靜失敗**(命令回 exit 0 但檔案冇出、或者成頁文字消失)。

## 五個坑(全部係實跑撞出嚟,唔係推測)

| # | 坑 | 徵狀 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 上游 `office/soffice.py` 用 `socket.AF_UNIX` 探測沙箱 | Windows 冇呢個屬性 → `recalc` / `thumbnail` / `accept_changes` **未做嘢就死** |
| 2 | `soffice.exe` 唔等轉換完成 | **exit 0 但檔案冇出現** |
| 3 | app flag `--calc` 撞 `-env:UserInstallation` | soffice crash `0xC0000409` |
| 4 | Python 預設 locale 編碼(cp950)讀 UTF-8 XML | **凡文件含中文就爆** `charmap codec can't decode` —— 對呢個全繁中嘅項目等於功能唔存在 |
| 5 | `NODE_PATH` 空,搵唔到 npm global 模組 | `require('docx')` → `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`(上游話「preinstalled 直接 require」喺呢度唔成立) |

另外 `zip` / `unzip` 兩個都冇(docx/pptx 編輯流程靠佢哋拆包重組),已用 `ooxml.py` 補上。

## 設計取態

**唔改 plugin cache** —— 而係喺載入上游 script 之前,換走壞咗嗰一個模組(`office.soffice`),其餘原封執行。

好處:plugin 更新照樣受惠,亦唔使維護一份會 drift 嘅分叉。實作見 `scripts/skillrun.py` 嘅 `install_shim()`(註冊入 `sys.modules`,但保留 `office` package 真實 `__path__`,所以 `office.validators` 等其他子模組照常載入)。

## 檔案

| 檔案 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | 五個坑 + 命令對照表(上游寫法 → 呢度寫法)+ 中文專屬注意 + 項目風格 |
| `scripts/win_soffice.py` | Windows LibreOffice runner(鎖 `.com`、隔走 crash flag、驗產出檔真存在) |
| `scripts/skillrun.py` | Launcher:動態搵 plugin 目錄(hash 會變)、注入 shim、UTF-8 re-exec |
| `scripts/ooxml.py` | OOXML 拆包 / 重組(代 `zip`/`unzip`;防 zip-slip 同 symlink) |
| `scripts/render.py` | 文件 → 逐頁圖(視覺 QA;會清走同名舊圖) |
| `scripts/nodegen.ps1` | 跑 node 生成腳本,自動補 `NODE_PATH` |

## 驗證 scenario(全部真跑過)

四個格式都行足「生成 → validate → 讀返 → 渲染睇圖」:

- **xlsx** — `recalc.py` 真經 LibreOffice 計算,讀返 `B5=253` / `B6=120` 正確(連 `_xlfn.MAXIFS` 前綴路徑都評估到)
- **docx** — `validate.py` PASSED;`ooxml.py` 拆包重組後**再 validate 依然 PASSED**
- **pptx** — `validate.py` `All validations PASSED!`,native chart 正常
- **pdf** — 繁中 + 上下標(H₂O、x²+y²)正確渲染
- `nodegen.ps1` — 喺清空 `NODE_PATH` 嘅環境照樣造到檔

第二個 commit 修一個實戰撞出嚟嘅 bug:UTF-8 re-exec 用 `os.execv`,但 Windows 冇真正嘅 exec,Python 唔會幫帶空格嘅參數加引號 ⇒ 「Azure UAT 部署流程 v1.0.docx」散成四個參數。改用 `subprocess`(經 `list2cmdline` quote)。

## 唔涉及

- 零 runtime dependency 改動(`apps/api` / `apps/web` 完全冇碰)—— 純 agent tooling,H2 不觸發
- 唯一 repo 改動:`.gitignore` 加 `__pycache__/` / `*.pyc`(Python helper 跑完會留 bytecode)

## 已知限制

- Word 目錄係功能變數,**LibreOffice 渲染出嚟係空白**。已設 `updateFields`,Word 開檔應該會更新 —— 但**我冇 Word 所以驗證唔到自動更新真係生效**。
- `thumbnail.py` / `accept_changes.py` / `comment.py` / PDF 表單 / OCR **未實跑過**。理論上通(兩個共通坑已修,行同一個 launcher),但唔當已驗證。

author: pjm17971
body:
The **throughput half** of [PND-PROCPAR]. N worker threads, each holding a long-lived `Host`; the pool is a router. **No engine change was needed** — which is why this half went first: a plan is already JSON, a registry is a module both isolates import, and a result's columns cross as transferable buffers.

## Measured, and it corrects the assessment

`packages/process/scripts/perf-pool.mjs`, 32 requests, 8 workers, 10 cores:

| workload | per request | in-process | pool(8) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| distinct | 0.7 ms | 22 ms | 24 ms | **0.94×** |
| distinct | 2.4 ms | 77 ms | 29 ms | 2.61× |
| distinct | 57.6 ms | 1842 ms | 509 ms | **3.62×** |
| repeated | 0.1 ms | 2 ms | 14 ms | **0.14×** |
| repeated | 7.1 ms | 228 ms | 93 ms | 2.44× |

The note predicted "near-linear". **It isn't** — the ceiling is ~3.6×, and below ~1–2 ms per request the pool *loses*. Every answer is shipped whether or not it was cheap; caching and pooling **compete** (a repeat-heavy workload is served from the in-process memo for ~0.1 ms while the pool still pays full wire cost); and "jobs must be ≥10 ms" was over-generalised from a four-job probe. Correction recorded in the note, and the benchmark sweeps request size so callers find their own crossover.

## Two bugs found building it

- A worker dying **before any request** left the pool silently broken — only in-flight requests rejected, everything after hung forever. Now latches a fatal state. Deliberately does not self-heal: replacing a worker would discard its warm graph silently.
- The worker entry resolved to a `.ts` path when the package is loaded from source; `new Worker` fails async, so it presented as a hang. Now a named error at `start`.

## Review notes

- **New public surface**: `@pond-ts/process/pool` subpath, plus `columnBuffers` / `columnFromBuffers`. API.md rows added. Package is `private: true` / WIP, so this isn't a published-API commitment.
- **The identity test is the one to read** — a worker's answer must equal the in-process answer cell for cell, including the `undefined` warm-up head that only survives if the validity bitmap crosses intact.
- The pool test suite loads from `dist/` (a worker can't load TypeScript); `npm test` builds first via `test:dts`.
- `.prettierignore` gains two generated website dirs — building the site locally then running `npm run verify` produced 40 spurious failures. CI never saw them.

The **latency half** stays open and is now correctly diagnosed: `Node.compute` is the only producer of a node's value and is contractually pure, so a result computed in another isolate has nowhere to land. That injection seam is the real blocker; recorded in the breakout plan.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Added after the original description

The branch stayed open across several sessions and picked up three more
pieces. Recording them here because this body is the durable record.

### `withWorkers` — the same idea one layer down [PND-SCANKERN]

`HostPool` parallelises **whole requests**. This parallelises **one
study over one series**: a resident pool of workers over a
`SharedArrayBuffer` arena, with the main thread parked in
`Atomics.wait` for the ~61 µs barrier — which is what lets the studies
stay **synchronous**. Node-only by construction; browsers forbid
`Atomics.wait` on the main thread, and that is fine.

```ts
TimeSeries.fromArrow(table, { time: 'ts' })
  .withWorkers({ workers: 8 })   // may appear anywhere in the chain
  .sma({ period: 20 }).bollinger({ period: 20 })
```

**Single-threaded remains the default** — the main package never
imports this. Measured over 500k bars, 8 workers: `sma` 1.85×,
`bollinger` 1.92×, a three-study stack 2.00×, all within 5.1e-13 of
the sequential answer.

`parallelDispatches()` ships alongside it: acceleration is otherwise
invisible, since a declined pass returns the same answer, only slower
than you expected.

### `zScore` in a shifted frame [PND-SHIFTFRAME]

Found through the parallel work and **first documented as a
parallelism bug, which it was not**. `zScore` derived its numerator as
`value − rollingMean`; `ulp(1e15)` is `0.125`, so a window spanning ±3
left the deviation about three bits. The sequential path had identical
exposure — partitioning only made two equally-wrong answers visibly
disagree.

Worst relative error vs an exact reference, 200k rows:

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `1e15 + ((i%7)−3)` | 1.0e+0 | 4.1e-15 |
| `1e9 + sin` | 4.1e+0 | 4.9e-12 |
| random walk ≈100 | 3.9e-6 | 4.4e-11 |
| `1e12·(1+i/N)` trending | 9.0e-6 | 4.9e-15 |

**Two consequences worth flagging for review.** `zScore` values
change — by rounding error on ordinary data, and by a lot where they
were wrong. And `zScore` is **no longer accelerated by `withWorkers`**:
the stable kernel is not the shape the pool hooks, so it went from the
fastest parallel study (2.44×) to sequential. A 2.44× on an answer that
can be 100% wrong is not a speedup.

### `partitionBy` on a dictionary-encoded key

A dict-encoded string column already carries integer group keys;
`partitionBy` was re-deriving them. 1.4–2.0× on `partitionBy`,
4.8–7.9× on `distinctPartitionKeys`. `scripts/perf-partition.mjs`
covers contiguous **and** interleaved layouts deliberately — the
interleaved case is the one a naive run-length assumption breaks on.

## Review notes for the additions

- **`.withWorkers()` mounts a method on `TimeSeries`** (via the opt-in
  `@pond-ts/financial/parallel` subpath). Per CLAUDE.md that is the
  category needing human approval, not just an agent pass.
- **A Codex pass on the shifted-frame kernel found two real bugs**
  (`20639a4`): a fixed 1024-row rebuild interval was wrong at both ends
  — 1.7e-6 error at `period 2`, and `O(N + N·period/1024)` cost, 81 ms
  at `period 100k`. Rebuilding once per **window turnover** fixes both.
  Its third finding (changed gap semantics) did not reproduce.
- **Four tests were vacuous and are fixed.** The `withWorkers` suite
  imported studies from `src` and the pool from `dist` — different
  module graphs — so nine tests compared **sequential to sequential**.
  The replacement canary was `zScore` disagreeing with the sequential
  answer, which only worked *because the accelerated result was
  inferior* and evaporated when that was fixed; `parallelDispatches()`
  replaced it.
- Tests: 4,442 green across all packages after merging `main`.

## What

Green dot = the mode is on and the pipeline is actually running. Yellow = on, but no video is playing or the pipeline has not taken over. Red = off.

The passthrough button is removed from the popup, and any stored `passthrough` preference migrates to `off`.

## Why

A dot toggled the `hidden` attribute, but `.tab-dot { display: inline-block }` overrides the UA `[hidden] { display: none }` rule, so a green dot showed permanently regardless of state. Colour now keys off a `data-state` attribute the stylesheet matches on.

Passthrough presents the source unenhanced, which is a development aid rather than a user choice. The mode itself stays because the renderer falls back to it internally, and the real-video checkpoint that exercises capture-and-present in isolation from the models is the only coverage of that path — it now drives the mode via `FSRCNNX_SETMODE` through the existing `sendContentCommand` helper instead of by clicking a button that no longer exists.

## Testing

- `npm run check` exit 0 — 630 Node tests, 41 Python with 3 expected skips, plus the syntax/package/model/generated/reference/release gates
- The old tests asserted the `hidden` attribute rather than rendered state, which is why they passed while the UI was wrong. They now assert the attribute the stylesheet keys on, plus a markup contract test that fails if a dot ever regains a `hidden` attribute.
- Packaged Chromium validation is what actually exercises the reworked harness checkpoint; it cannot run locally here (Edge hands off to a running instance, Vivaldi closes the CDP connection).

author: benkuah
body:
## The problem

The detail panel's inline-edit save cue centred its bubble on the edited field's `<dd>`. That element spans the **whole panel column**, while the value inside it is usually a word or two — so the green "Saved" popped up over the empty right half of the row, pointing at nothing.

Measured on a real record in the browser: **the bubble's left edge sat 165px right of the value's left edge.** That defeats the entire reason the cue is anchored to the field rather than being a corner `Toast` — the confirmation is supposed to land where the user's eyes already are.

Centring isn't wrong in general, it's wrong *here*. For a table cell the anchor's box genuinely **is** the value, so centring is correct; for a panel field the anchor is a wide container around a short value.

## The change

`useSaveCue` gains an `align` option:

- **`'center'`** — unchanged default. The table cell (`Cell`) and every Gantt drag keep today's behaviour exactly; Gantt already anchors at the drop point via `pointAnchor`.
- **`'start'`** — `PanelField` opts in. Pins the bubble's **left edge** to the value's, and moves the arrow from the bubble's centre to a fixed 14px inset so it lands on the value's first characters rather than past the end of a short one.

Alignment moves **X only**. The 8px gap and the flip-below-when-near-the-viewport-top rule are unchanged and shared by both hosts.

Scoped to the detail panels by design — which covers **both** panel levels, since the tabbed L1 `RecordDetailPanel` and the flat L2/L3 `NestedDetailPanel` render every field through the one `PanelField`.

**The error state is deliberately untouched.** The red "Couldn't save · reverted" bubble and its `gem-cue-revert` blink behave exactly as before; they just inherit the new alignment like everything else.

## Testing

The placement maths came out of the component as a pure `saveCuePlacement(rect, align)`, so the rules are testable without a DOM — matching how `Modal`/`panelDismiss` are covered.

- **Unit (`SaveCue.test.ts`, 6 new cases)** — pins that start-alignment is **invariant to the anchor's width while centring is not**. That difference *is* the fix, so it's the assertion worth having. Also pins that alignment changes X only and that the flip-below rule still holds. FE suite: **477/477**.
- **Playwright** — the existing save-cue test now asserts the geometry live: the cue's left edge within 4px of the value's, **guarded by a check that the row is wider than the bubble**. Without that guard the two alignments would land in the same place on a narrow row and the assertion would prove nothing.
- **Negative-controlled** — reverting `PanelField` to the default alignment turns that test red (`Expected: < 4, Received: 164.8`), so it is load-bearing rather than vacuously green. Restored and re-verified.

Everything ran against an **isolated worktree stack** — its own Postgres, Redis and MinIO on their own ports, own compose project and volumes, nothing shared with the main stack:

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `record-panel-inline-edit.ui.spec.ts` | 6 passed |
| `qa:smoke` | 11 passed / 3 skipped |
| Gantt drag specs (assert *where* the shared cue lands) | 4 passed |
| `pnpm gate` | green — incl. `dotnet test` 135/135 + 230/230 |

The Gantt drag specs matter here specifically: `save-cue` is a single shared instance re-anchored per edit, so a wrong anchor still reads "Saved" and is invisible to a text assertion. Those specs assert its position, and they confirm the other surfaces are untouched.

## Docs

- `Docs/features/record-detail-panel.md` — §3.4 step 5, the §5 Saving/Save-success/Save-error rows, and a changelog entry.
- `Docs/REUSE.md` — the new `align` option on the `SaveCue` registry row, and a note to extend `saveCuePlacement` rather than the component if a third alignment is ever needed.
- `Docs/QA-PLAN.md` — per-surface cue placement is now asserted rather than assumed, plus the timing gotcha (capture `boundingBox()` before the slower text assertions eat the ~1.6s the cue is on screen).

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm gate` green
- [x] `pnpm format` run (touched files only, no unrelated churn)
- [x] Behaviour change ships with its test, at the unit **and** Playwright tiers
- [x] Owning feature doc updated (Status + changelog)
- [x] No new `api.ts` method, no new endpoint, no schema or seed change
- [x] No secrets in the diff

author: collectorscampus
body:
Adds a `listing.sku` capability, a Shopify implementation, and an opt-in on match confirmation.

## Why

With the catalogue id in the storefront's own SKU field, the *mapping* stops living only in this database. A hub rebuilt from nothing re-derives every link from the platform, instead of asking the operator to match 1,300 items again. It also promotes future matches from a name resemblance to an exact id — the `certain` path that can be accepted in bulk.

Measured on the live store, this is the missing piece: every match came back `possible · partial name`, because the titles are prefixed ("Pokémon TCG: Scarlet & Violet Surging Sparks Elite Trainer Box") and tcgcsv's are not. `certain` was 0 and stays 0 until something carries a TCGPlayer id.

## It overwrites, and that is the whole risk

The operator's variants already carry a live internal scheme — `191-87991`, `191-41312`, `100-10013`, `100-10623`; two prefix families, populated on **every** variant sampled. This replaces them. That was raised with the evidence and **explicitly authorised**.

The code is built so it cannot happen by accident:

- **Off unless the request asks.** Mutation checked: removing the opt-in condition fails exactly the test that protects those codes, and nothing else.
- **Only ever applied to a listing whose link was just confirmed.** Nothing is written for an unmatched or ambiguous row.
- **Asking a connector that cannot do it is an error, not a silent no-op.** Telling an operator their ids were recorded when nothing was written is the worst available outcome.
- **An empty SKU is refused in the connector.** Shopify would accept it and the seller's code would simply be gone.
- **The checkbox defaults off, is not remembered between runs**, and states the consequence in bold at the point of decision rather than in documentation nobody reads.

## Ordering is deliberate

The channel is written only **after** the link is recorded locally. The reverse would leave the storefront stamped with an id this hub has no allocation for — a lie that survives a restart and that reconciliation has no way to explain. Pinned by a test that fails the local step and asserts nothing was written.

There is one case worth naming: an *unchanged* link (already exactly as requested) still gets the stamp. That is intentional — the write is idempotent on the platform, and it makes a half-finished run completable rather than requiring the operator to unlink first.

## Shopify specifics

A variant's SKU lives on its **inventory item**, so this goes through `productVariantsBulkUpdate` with `inventoryItem: { sku }` — the same mutation and the same `write_products` scope the price write already uses, confirmed against the Admin API docs.

Written **verbatim**, with a test asserting `00704143` is not tidied to `704143`. The matcher's certain path is an equality test; a connector that normalised the value would quietly turn tomorrow's exact match back into a name guess.

Rate limited through the connector's declared limit, as reconciliation does it — Shopify allows 2/s and a batch of forty confirmations would otherwise burst straight through it.

## How it was verified

- **409 API tests, 87 Shopify, 59 SDK** — all green, plus `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check` and `build`, against Postgres on 5433 and Redis on 6380.
- Mutation checked on the opt-in guard, as above.
- **No live write performed.** The read-only half of this workflow was driven against the real store earlier in the session; stamping SKUs onto real variants is the operator's call to make, from the UI, with the warning in front of them.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm test` passes
- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` **and `pnpm format:check`** all pass
- [x] `schema.prisma` untouched
- [x] No credentials, real shop domains, account ids or seller names in any tracked file

body:
## 문제

이전 PR(#108) 이후에도 **"이용권 확인이 다 안 됐는데 스플래시가 끝난다"** 가 남았다.
원인은 `auth` 준비 신호를 **'확인 종료'가 아닌 지점에서** 쏘고 있었던 것이다.

## 원인 3가지 (전부 코드로 특정)

### 1. `__cdRenderAuthSubscriptionDelay(true)` 가 `auth` 를 발행 — 주원인

이 렌더는 "확인 종료"가 아니라 **"서버가 미확정으로 답했고 재시도가 예약됐다"** 는 뜻이다.
호출부 3곳(`index.html` 3.5초 타이머 / 구독 응답 미확정 / 1800ms 후속) **전부 직후에
`__cdScheduleSubscriptionRetry(6500)` 를 건다.**

`degraded`·401/403 같은 **흔한 일시 오류**에 서버가 300ms 만에 답하면 → 즉시 `delay(true)`
→ `auth` 발행 → **스플래시가 0.3초 만에 걷히고 "이용권 확인이 지연되고 있어요" 카드가 그대로 노출.**

→ 신호 제거. 진행 바만 한 칸 올려(`__cdBootProgressNudge`) 굳어 보이지 않게 한다.

### 2. `__cdRenderGuestAuthLinks()` 가 프로브 대기 중에도 `auth` 를 발행

로컬 캐시 없는 **쿠키 세션**은 `!t && !us` 로 들어와 게스트로 먼저 그려지고, 그 다음
`__cdScheduleGuestProbe()` 로 신원을 확인한다. 그 **잠정** 렌더에서 신호를 쏘면
로그인 사용자인데도 게스트 시점에 스플래시가 걷힌다.

→ `pendingProbe` 옵션으로 억제. 프로브가 끝난 뒤(인증 시 `__cdAuthState()` 재실행,
미인증 시 이 함수 재호출) 확정 시점에 발행한다.

### 3. 하드 상한 3.5초가 재시도 결과보다 짧았다

미확정 뒤 재시도는 **6.5초 후**에 답을 낸다. 상한이 그보다 짧으면
"재시도가 답을 내기 직전에 스플래시만 걷히는" 구간이 생긴다(3.5초가 정확히 그랬다).

→ **8초**로 상향. 정상 경로는 1초 안쪽이라 예외 상황에서만 관여한다.

## 검증

시나리오 단정 10개 — 셸의 실제 함수를 그대로 떼어내 jsdom 에서 실행:

- 지연 표시(재시도 예약)로는 **걷히지 않음** ★
- 프로브 대기 중 잠정 게스트 렌더로는 **걷히지 않음** ★
- 4.2초(구 상한 초과)·6.8초(재시도 시점)에도 유지, **8초 상한에는 해제**(무한 대기 금지) ★
- 확정 카드가 그려지면 해제 / 비로그인은 종전대로 즉시 해제(회귀 없음)
- 대기 중 진행 바가 움직임

`verify:auth-event-loop` 가드에 세 결함을 각각 못박는 단정 추가
(지연 렌더의 신호 발행 금지 / `pendingProbe` 억제 존재 / 상한 ≥ 7500ms).

전체 게이트 통과: `auth-event-loop`·`public-parity`·`locale-main-sync`·`billing-pass-policy`·
`paid-gate-ui`·`portone-single-payment`·`paid-feature-billing-policy`·`runtime-cache-sync`·`typecheck`.

## 트레이드오프

이용권 확인이 **일시 오류로 한 번 실패한 경우** 스플래시가 최대 8초까지 유지된다
(재시도 결과를 기다리는 것이 요구사항). 정상 경로는 영향 없다.

body:
## Summary

Extracts gtm-agent's shipped vault safety guard (gtm#612 — 48 production vault files tombstoned by a half-mounted sandbox that scanned cleanly) into a shared, server-safe, **zero-import** policy subpath `./vault/server`, per the #332 audit verdict that these two checks are universal shell mechanism:

- **`assessVaultDeletionBatch`** — blast-radius deletion refusal: refuses an empty-manifest batch, an all-files wipe (at ANY count), or a ratio/floor breach (`>= 0.75` of `>= 10` live files — both `>=`, byte-matching gtm). gtm's constants are exported (`VAULT_DELETION_REFUSAL_RATIO`, `VAULT_DELETION_REFUSAL_MIN_LIVE_FILES`) so gtm can delete its local copies. Refusal is a verdict, not a throw — what to do with it stays the caller's.
- **`compareIncarnationBaseline`** — fail-closed filesystem-incarnation comparison over structural fields (`FilesystemIncarnationLike`, no `@tangle-network/sandbox` import): `unidentified` → `not-ready` → `no-baseline` → `mismatch` → `match`, each earlier check short-circuiting the later ones.

New entry wired in `tsup.config.ts` + `package.json` `exports` + `knip.json` (no root barrel exists). `tests/browser-safe-subpaths.test.ts` auto-excludes it (server-only; deliberately NOT added to `BROWSER_NONREACT`).

## API refinements vs the issue's proposed surface

Three deliberate deltas from #331's sketch (its surface is explicitly a proposal):

1. **`manifestEmpty?: boolean` input** — the two-list shape `{baselinePaths, proposedDeletions}` cannot distinguish `'empty-manifest'` from `'all-files'` (an empty scan structurally implies all-files). One boolean recovers gtm's diagnostic distinction; when `true`, the FULL baseline is treated as would-delete regardless of `proposedDeletions` (fail-closed — an empty scan means nothing survived). gtm's drop-in stays one call: `{ baselinePaths: liveBaselinePaths, proposedDeletions: wouldDeletePaths, manifestEmpty: manifest.entries.size === 0 }`; deletion-list-first adopters (legal/creative) simply omit it.
2. **`wouldDeletePaths: string[]` output** (sorted, mirroring gtm's `.sort()`) — gtm logs these on refusal; callers need them for surfacing. Reason precedence when several fire: `empty-manifest` > `all-files` > `ratio-exceeded`.
3. **`{ verdict: 'no-baseline' }`** added as a 5th verdict — gtm treats `baseline_missing` as a distinct state with distinct remediation; forcing callers to pre-gate on `baselineId === undefined` reintroduces a forgettable judgment call (`baselineId ?? ''` would misroute to `'mismatch'`). An exhaustive `switch` now gets compile-time coverage.

## Test plan

- `tests/vault/server.test.ts` (27 tests): gtm-parity fixture matrix reproducing gtm's own equivalence-test fixtures (1-live all-files, 11-live blast-radius with 10 refused paths, 2-live legit delete, empty manifest, 95-live nearly-empty as `ratio-exceeded` NOT `all-files`, 20-live single delete, 3-live ratio-floor) + operator-exactness boundaries (ratio exactly 0.75 refused; 0.7 allowed; 0.889 at count 9 allowed) + precedence + policy override + constants + incarnation matrix incl. both fail-closed precedence properties.

body: ## Change class Runtime packaging (Musea static export + preview runtime). ## How the a11y panel works The A11y panel does not read pre-baked results — it runs axe live in the browser. The gallery posts `musea:run-a11y` into the preview iframe, the preview loads `/vendor/axe-core.min.js`, runs `axe.run` on the `.musea-variant` container, and posts `musea:a11y-result` back. `useA11y` keys pending requests by `requestId` and times them out after 30s. axe-core is an **optional peer**, and both ends were best-effort about that. In a deployed static gallery, that combination makes the whole feature fail without a usable signal. ## Defect 1 — the export silently ships no axe `emitAxeVendor` swallowed an unresolvable axe-core and emitted nothing: ```ts } catch { // axe-core is an optional peer; static a11y keeps the same best-effort behavior as dev. } ``` The exported gallery then has no vendor script at all, and the build prints nothing. The first sign of trouble is a user clicking **Run** in the deployed panel. Nothing in the test suite covered the asset either, so a regression here was invisible. ## Defect 2 — a load event is treated as proof axe exists ```js await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { script.onload = resolve; script.onerror = reject; document.head.appendChild(script); }); // ... const results = await window.axe.run(context, { ... }); ``` Dev answers the vendor route with a **404**, so `onerror` fires and the runner reports a load failure — that path is fine. A static host is free to answer a missing asset with an **SPA fallback: 200 plus HTML**, which is the default on several common hosts. The script tag then "loads" successfully, `window.axe` stays `undefined`, and `window.axe.run` fails with: ``` Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'run') ``` which points nowhere near the missing dependency. This is the deployed-only failure: identical code works in dev because dev returns a real 404. ## Fix - Warn at build time when axe-core cannot be resolved, naming the install command, so the omission is visible where it is actionable rather than in a user's browser. - Verify `window.axe` after the load event and throw an error that names both the cause and the remedy (install axe-core; check the path is served as JavaScript rather than an SPA fallback). The existing catch path already posts `musea:a11y-result` with the `requestId`, so the gallery renders the message immediately instead of spinning until its 30s timeout. ## Tests `static-export.test.ts` — pins that the export ships `__musea__/vendor/axe-core.min.js` and that the asset is really axe-core rather than an empty or placeholder file. Previously uncovered. `addons.test.ts` (new) — pins the runtime contract in the generated preview script: - the `window.axe` check exists **after** the load await, not just the load event; - the message names the missing dependency, so it is actionable; - the message mentions the served-as-HTML case, which is specifically how a deployed gallery hits this; - the catch path still posts `musea:a11y-result` carrying the `requestId`, so a failure cannot degrade into the 30s timeout. Reverting `addons.ts` fails the first of these with `the runner must verify window.axe after the vendor script loads, not just await the load event`. ## Verification ```sh cd npm/builder/vite-musea vp exec tsx --test src/preview/addons.test.ts src/static-export.test.ts vp check src ``` - 8 tests pass. - `vp check`: 105 files formatted, no lint errors in 102 files. ## Note `handleArtA11y` in `src/api-routes/handlers.ts` is a stub that always returns `{ violations: [], passes: 0, incomplete: 0 }` ("populated after VRT --a11y run"), and `createStaticGalleryPayload` bakes its output into `static.json` under `details[art].a11y`. The panel does not read that field — it runs axe live — so this PR does not change it. But it means `fetchA11y` reports "no violations" for every component in a static gallery, which is a false pass for any consumer that does read it. Worth its own issue; I did not want to change the payload shape inside a fix for the runtime path. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is enabled.

- **Hooks**: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse/PostToolUse (Bash), Stop — captured into the same local `~/.aka/data/aka.db`.
- **The full setup wizard** (calibration → triage → remediation), shared with Claude Code via `@akasecurity/setup-wizard` (parent PR). The judge spawns `codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --output-last-message <tmp> -` with the prompt on stdin; `--ephemeral` keeps the judge session out of `~/.codex/sessions` so AKA's own backfill can never re-ingest raw findings.
- **History backfill** sweeps prior Codex rollout files (`~/.codex/sessions`) with the same triage-stream contract, self-contamination guard, and dedup.
- **Model-judge privacy parity**: the judge sends the same minimized `toJudgePayload` projection as Claude Code (rawMatch legible, context re-masked, `filePath`/`valueFingerprint`/`keyVersion` dropped before egress), gated on the same distinct `modelJudgeConsent` opt-in, with the disclosure collected by the skill before anything crosses.
- **Semantics adopted from main's vault line** (the parts that apply without vault wiring): a redact-policy **prompt now blocks** instead of warning-and-passing the raw secret to the model; a vault **pointer in an executable field denies** the call in every consent state (pointers minted by the Claude Code plugin on the same machine can reach Codex Bash commands); the judge refuses to run without an injected spawn seam and a cleanup fault can't displace the real error.

## Deliberate deferrals (flagged, not hidden)

- **The vault is not wired for Codex** this round. The shared runtime never vaults on its own, so Codex captures stay one-way-redacted (the safe direction); the setup skill's Known-limitation section discloses this, including that pointers render as literal `[[aka:...]]` tokens in Codex output (Codex has no display-side hook equivalent to MessageDisplay). A follow-up can port the consent step + rollout scrubber as a package.
- Codex fires PreToolUse/PostToolUse only for `Bash` today, not `apply_patch` — the file-write entry is registered but inert upstream (tracking issue referenced in-source); backfill covers file content after the fact.
- The judge spawn shape is verified against the openai/codex source and pinned by tests with injected spawns; it has not been exercised against a live `codex` binary in CI.
- The Security page's `codex` row is set to coverage 80 / supported (judgment call reflecting the Bash-only hook gap) and pinned by a repository test.
- The plugin registers through the in-repo marketplace; listing in the external marketplace repo is a follow-up outside this tree.

Versions stay on main's 0.9.3 line — the 0.10.0 bump is the last PR of this stack.

## Verification

Full workspace `turbo run typecheck lint test` green at this tip (the plugin's suite includes built-script e2e tests: the enforcement matrix through the real prompt hook, the no-consent journey proving no `codex` subprocess spawns without the opt-in, pointer-deny before store-open, onboarding consent read-back, version lockstep). `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` clean; dependency-audit gates pass.

## Post-draft deep review (internal) — applied

- The judge spawn now pins `stdio` explicitly: execFileSync's default teed the `codex exec` child's stderr into the parent command's stderr (the wizard transcript the backfill later scans). A journey test proves a stub judge's stderr logging never surfaces. The Claude Code judge on main has the same latent (lower-exposure) gap — flagged as a follow-up, not touched here.
- The executable-field pointer-deny copy no longer sends users to `aka exception approve` (this plugin never substitutes pointers); it points at `aka vault show` / the dashboard instead.
- The first-run nudge names the real skill (`aka-setup`); the release workflow's header and missing `concurrency:` group are fixed; the model-judge consent copy states the grant is machine-wide across harnesses; CLAUDE.md's env-opt-out table and release section are updated.

**Release prerequisite (not in this diff):** `@akasecurity/ai-tc-codex` is a new npm name with no Trusted Publisher — configure it for `release-plugin-codex.yml` on npmjs.com (or bootstrap-publish once) before the first `plugin-codex-v*` tag, or the publish fails masked as a 404. Also note the in-repo marketplace entry goes live when this merges, while the npm package appears only at the 0.10.0 tag — keep that window short.

## Résumé
`is_safe_external_url` ne bloquait le link-local que pour les IPv4 littérales (`169.254.0.0/16`). Deux contournements SSRF subsistaient :
- **IPv4-mapped IPv6** : `::ffff:169.254.169.254` atteignait l'endpoint metadata cloud (issue #733).
- **IPv6 link-local natif** : `fe80::/10` n'était pas filtré (asymétrie avec l'IPv4).

Ce fix normalise les adresses IPv4-mapped vers leur IPv4 sous-jacente, puis bloque tout le link-local via `ip.is_link_local` (couvre `169.254.0.0/16` **et** `fe80::/10`). La politique produit d'autoriser le LAN domestique (127.x, 10.x, 192.168.x, unique-local IPv6) est préservée.

## Détails
- `cinesort/infra/network_utils.py` : restructuration du bloc de validation IP.

|-----|---------|
| `http://192.168.1.50:8096` | autorisé |
| `http://[2001:4860:4860::8888]/` | autorisé |
| `http://169.254.169.254/` | bloqué |
| `http://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/` | bloqué (link-local) |
| `http://[fe80::1]:8096/` | bloqué (link-local) |

Closes #733

body: Replaces two hand-rolled provider adapters with a single inference path on the Vercel AI SDK v6, routed through OpenRouter with one BYOK key, and puts web search behind a swappable `SearchProvider` interface. Implements `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-openrouter-migration-design.md`. ## Proven live, not just green offline One live research run against a real company (Linear) with a real OpenRouter key: | | | |---|---| | sections | **7/7 populated** | | claims | 33, **29 cited** — fill rate 0.879 | | citations | 29, **27 resolved** (93%) | | real web searches | 15 | | **measured cost** | **~$0.085–0.14** vs ~$1.00 baseline | Cost range rather than a point estimate: the 7/7 run benefited from a warm search cache seeded by the previous run, which measured 0.1417. **Quote ~$0.14**, the conservative end — it matches the spec's projection. A **7–12x reduction**. Offline: **250 tests / 31 files green, `tsc --noEmit` clean.** ## What changed - **Inference** — `adapters/anthropic.ts`, `adapters/kimi.ts`, `provider.ts` and the whole `llm/tools/` tree deleted. One path: `generateText` + tools, against a hardcoded two-tier map (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite` for disambiguation and six sections, `deepseek-v4-pro` for moat). `FS_MODEL_DEFAULT` / `FS_MODEL_REASONING` override for eval sweeps only. - **Search** — new `src/lib/search/` with a `SearchProvider` interface and EXA, Firecrawl and Tavily implementations. Budget, cache, retry, source-fallback and usage counting live in one `withSearchPolicy` wrapper every provider passes through. - **BYOK** — one OpenRouter key plus one search key. Anthropic and Kimi key handling removed, with a localStorage purge for stale entries. - **Evals** — Evalite harness, 20-company golden set split 10 early-stage / 10 enterprise, four deterministic scorers. Gated behind `npm run eval`, never in CI, never yet run. - **Review gates** — CodeRabbit on PRs into `main` only; `dev` stays ungated so the integration branch does not stall. ## Six defects that a fully green offline suite did not catch Every one of these was found only by running against a real key. Recorded in `tasks/todo.md`. 1. **Tool name mismatch** — every prompt says `web_search`; the loop registered `exa_search`. All 8 calls were told to use a tool that did not exist. 2. **Timeout scope inversion** — `TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` was carried over verbatim, but the old adapter applied it *per turn* across ≤12 turns while the new one wrapped the entire tool loop. Same constant, ~12x less headroom. 3. **Missing `SearchBudget`** — the policy wrapper required a budget the tool loop never passed; every search died on a `TypeError` before reaching the network. 4. **Invalid search key** — 401 on every search, masked as "budget exhausted" because only the *last* error was reported rather than the first. 5. **`Output.object` forces a response format on tool steps** — the SDK attaches it to every step, so the model cannot emit a tool call and instead complies immediately with a schema-valid *empty* object. This is why sections "succeeded" with zero claims, and why `moat` appeared to work while never searching: its citations were model memory. `usage.calls = 0` was accurate the whole time. 6. **Flat per-step timeout across tiers** — a reasoning model's thinking phase legitimately exceeds 60s. ## Review gates run - `/simplify` — 4 parallel agents. Fixed: a second stale `exa_search` string that reached the model at budget exhaustion; `withRetry` re-paying for entire tool loops on timeout; user-facing copy still naming Anthropic and Kimi; dead retry aliases; two Supabase writes serialised in front of the fan-out. - `/security-review` — no HIGH or MEDIUM findings. Two candidates investigated and filtered as below-threshold, then fixed anyway: unpaired search key/provider headers could route the operator's EXA key to Tavily, and the settings Save button was not gated on auth hydration. ## Known gaps - **Phase C1 not started** — per-section `includeDomains` grounding and the first eval run. The harness exists but has never been run, so ~$0.14 is one company, not a benchmark. - **Settings UI has no live click-through** — markup proven by server-rendering the component; the hydrated behaviours (load-time purge, toasts, readiness line) are unverified against a real session. - `exaCompanyLogo` reads `process.env.EXA_API_KEY` and bypasses the policy wrapper, so Firecrawl/Tavily users get no logo. - Firecrawl/Tavily response parsing is not null-tolerant the way EXA's now is. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_012mpqo7S27mDdSP6GigkRLD > [!NOTE] > ### Migrate LLM inference to OpenRouter with swappable search providers, BYOK, and eval scaffolding > - Replaces Anthropic/Kimi SDK with the AI SDK v4 + `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider`; all research calls now route through [`src/lib/llm/openrouter.ts`](https://github.com/abhaypadmanabhan/FounderScope/pull/1/files#diff-43c7a9ce53d1d952685610d9ffe7ca08ff3185d8536d2815c7e477bdc37e9f65) with two model tiers (`default`/`reasoning`) configurable via env vars. > - Adds a pluggable search layer in [`src/lib/search/`](https://github.com/abhaypadmanabhan/FounderScope/pull/1/files#diff-a0ddc4b11794834b8cdda0af14086690685f9d23fa7ca466321132f7b74ad546) supporting EXA, Firecrawl, and Tavily with budget enforcement, Supabase caching, source fallback, and 429 retry logic. > - Replaces Anthropic/Kimi API key management with OpenRouter + search provider keys in [`src/lib/api-keys.ts`](https://github.com/abhaypadmanabhan/FounderScope/pull/1/files#diff-b908a5ad7dc9108d0fee7fb66c4486c212929c5bba686b6d985075476e25d453); settings UI and research page updated accordingly; old Anthropic/Kimi keys are purged from localStorage on load. > - Adds an Evalite-based eval harness under [`evals/`](https://github.com/abhaypadmanabhan/FounderScope/pull/1/files#diff-f028e06aeef52b785823f751d3bc059eb306fba0df35ba76d67671f2143b60d1) with a golden set of 20 companies, deterministic scorers (schema pass, citation fill-rate, dead-link rate, domain adherence), and fixture data; eval tasks are scaffolded but not yet wired. > - Risk: `runResearchCall` now unconditionally routes to OpenRouter; the previous Anthropic/Kimi dispatch paths are deleted and cannot be restored without code changes. > > > > Macroscope summarized d80515e. > >

## 무엇을 고쳤나

**커버리지를 한 번도 측정한 적이 없었다.** 처음 재니 68.3% 인데, `coverage.all` 없이 재면 **86.5% 로 보인다** — 테스트가 한 번도 import 하지 않은 파일은 istanbul 리포트에 아예 안 실리기 때문이다.

그렇게 빠진 26개 파일에 `app/api/auth/callback/chzzk/route.ts`(42 stmt)가 있었다. 그 파일은 **유닛도 e2e 도 안 본다** — e2e 로그인은 치지직 OAuth 를 안 태우고 access 쿠키를 직접 서명하므로(ADR-0021) 콜백 경로를 지나가지 않는다. 도구가 없어서 안 보였고, 잘못 켰으면 여전히 안 보였을 자리다.

## 실측

| 영역 | statements | 비고 |
|---|---|---|
| `src/core` | 94.5% | 도메인·머신 |
| `src/features` | 94.1% | 유즈케이스·라우터 |
| `src/app` | 48.9% | API 라우트 5개 전부 0% |

## 결정 셋

- **커버리지는 항상 켜져 있다**(`enabled: true`). 별도 스크립트로 빼면 로컬 `npm test` 와 CI 판정이 갈려 "로컬에서 게이트를 그대로 돌린다"가 깨진다. 8.6s → 10.5s(실측).
- **provider 는 `istanbul`.** 기본값 v8 은 `node:inspector` Session 을 쓰는데 workerd 엔 없다 — 워커 풀 스펙 35개가 `ERR_METHOD_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` 로 죽고 리포트가 dom 프로젝트만 담은 32% 로 나온다(실측).
- **임계치는 목표가 아니라 래칫**(바닥). 현재 수치 바로 아래에 박고 테스트를 늘리는 PR 이 같이 올린다. 목표치를 미리 박으면 숫자를 채우려는 테스트가 섞이는데, 이 저장소의 테스트는 대부분 "실제로 터진 것"을 못박은 것들이다(`migration-0007.spec.ts` 가 전형).

## ADR-0029 — 검증 다섯 층

지뢰 목록이 네 번 반복하는 **"게이트가 전부 초록인데 이건 안 잡힌다"** 의 답은 게이트를 조이는 게 아니라 **층을 얹는 것**이다. 각 층이 무엇을 보고 **무엇을 구조적으로 못 보는지**까지 표로 못박았다.

| # | 층 | 못 보는 것 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 유닛 · workerd | DOM, `fs`, 실제 HTTP |
| 2 | 유닛 · dom | 서버 계약(tRPC 목), 레이아웃·색 |
| 3 | e2e · `next dev` | **`caches` 등 workerd 전역** |
| 4 | e2e · workerd preview | 실제 CPU 한도, 엣지 캐시 |
| 5 | 배포 후 · 프로덕션 스모크 | 되돌리지 않는다 — 사람이 판단 |

층 4·5 와 axe 접근성 스캔은 후속 PR 이다. 이 PR 은 층 1·2 의 측정과 래칫, 그리고 표 자체를 세운다.

## 게이트에 이빨이 있는지

author: electrohyun
body:
## Summary

Real socket.io passes a reason to `disconnect` listeners and lets the server close a socket with `socket.disconnect(close?)`. smocket did neither: the `disconnect` event fired with no argument, the client never fired `disconnect` at all, and there was no server-initiated path.

This adds `ServerSocketContract.disconnect(close?)` and routes a reason to both sides:

| trigger | client `disconnect` | server `disconnect` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.disconnect()` | `io client disconnect` | `client namespace disconnect` |
| `serverSocket.disconnect()` | `io server disconnect` | `server namespace disconnect` |

`close` only decides whether the transport is torn down too, which a mock does not have, so it is accepted and ignored. Delivery still goes through the single `defer`, so `disconnecting` precedes `disconnect` and per-socket order holds.

The reason strings were read off the real target with a throwaway probe and pinned in dual-run tests, not guessed ([0000](https://github.com/electrohyun/smocket/blob/main/docs/decisions/0000-do-not-invent-what-has-no-source.md)). Out of scope and untouched: WebSocket close codes, ping/pong, heartbeat, framing (0009, scope.md). Heartbeat-derived reasons such as `ping timeout` cannot arise in a transport-less mock and are not reproduced.

## Related issue

Closes #81

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Behavior verified against real socket.io

The new tests in `disconnect.test.ts` were pinned against the real target first (they pass there) and drive both targets to the same reasons; both are green.

## Summary

Makes delegation **brain-agnostic** and gives the hosted (Medulla) cognition path delegation, which it entirely lacked — on smoke1 and every hosted tenant the orchestrator could not delegate at all (its catalog was only `manifest.tools.allow` and `CycleHostImpl::call_tool` had no delegation arm). Closes the core of #176.

- **RunTurn seam** — lifts delegation orchestration out of `HarnessBrain` behind a `RunTurn` trait (`src/runtime/delegation.rs`) + `HarnessRunTurn` impl; the harness path is behavior-preserving.
- **Shared primitives** — new non-gated `src/runtime/delegation_tools.rs`: canonical tool names, argument schemas, the hosted `ToolManifestEntry` catalog, and the desk-lead resolver — one definition for both brains (the harness orchestrator re-exports them, drift-safe).
- **Hosted delegation (durable async hand-off)** — the builder advertises `spawn_task`/`delegate_to_desk` to Medulla; `CycleHostImpl` services them device-side: `spawn_task` opens a board card; `delegate_to_desk` resolves the desk and writes a durable hand-off card assigned to it (lead noted), unknown desk = clean tool error. A hosted build has no in-process cognition pool, so this is a durable **asynchronous** hand-off, not a synchronous in-voice relay.
- **Handed-task awareness (#176 scope C)** — when an operator message is addressed to a desk/agent that owns open work, the kernel folds a briefing of that work into the message the brain sees (brain-agnostic; mutates only the in-memory copy, never the durable log), so a direct "what are you working on?" is answered truthfully.

### Scope boundary (honest)

- The **synchronous** cross-agent cognition relay and recursive desk depth are **not** in this PR — a hosted build runs no local cognition, so a live desk reply needs either a core-in-pod build (`openhuman` feature) or Medulla multi-agent sub-cycles. Verified live that the **core-in-pod** build already does the full loop (CEO → desk → one-voice relay, and the follow-up answers).
- This branch carries one base-dependency commit — `0fd01f6` ("relay delegate_to_desk answer through a second orchestrator turn", the #175 relay) — which is not yet in `main` and has no open PR; the seam refactor builds on it. Flagging so a maintainer can decide whether to land it here or separately.

## API Or Behavior Changes

- Hosted brain now advertises and services `spawn_task` / `delegate_to_desk` (new device tools) — previously unavailable on the hosted path.
- Addressed operator messages may carry an in-memory handed-work briefing to the brain; the durable event log is unchanged.
- Harness (openhuman) path is behavior-preserving.

## 概要

OpenAI Game Studio プラグイン（v0.1.2）の `playtest-checklist.md` に沿ってブラウザ実機QAを実施し、見つかった問題に対応した。

プラグインは Codex 形式のため Claude Code のスキルとしては直接ロードできないが、ガイダンス（`skills/game-ui-frontend`、`skills/game-playtest`、`references/playtest-checklist.md`）を読み、その基準とワークフローに従って検証した。3D/Phaser 系のスキルは本プロジェクト（既存の React/DOM ベース 2D ゲーム）には非該当のため使っていない。

## 検出した問題と対応

### 1. タブ離脱中もタイマーが進む（実害あり）

**プレイヤーが見るもの**: ゲーム中に別のタブを見て戻ると、時間が減っている（3秒離脱で3秒減少を実測）。

**なぜ問題か**: 子どもが席を離れたり、先生が別画面を見せている間にも時間切れになり、スコアが不当に下がる。学習ツールとして体験を損なう。

**対応**: `visibilitychange` で `playing` → `paused` にする。戻ったときの自動再開はしない（不意にゲームが動き出さないよう、再開は本人の操作に任せる）。

### 2. framer-motion が reduced-motion 設定を見ていない

`globals.css` は CSS アニメーションに `prefers-reduced-motion` 対応済みだが、framer-motion が JS で書き込む transform には効かない。`MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` で OS 設定を尊重するようにした。

> **補足**: 当初のプレイテストで「reduced-motion 違反」を検出したが、これは**計測ミスによる誤検知**だった（1px のレイアウト確定をアニメーションと判定していた）。実際には transform は両モードとも `none` で、視覚的な問題はなかった。`MotionConfig` は将来 transform アニメーションを足したときの保険として残している。誤検知を招いた E2E は削除した。

### 3. E2E の安定性

| 問題 | 対応 |
| --- | --- |
| 性能テストが12並列では毎回失敗（開発サーバーの応答遅延で first-paint が閾値超え。単独なら6件とも通過） | `e2e-perf/` と専用 config に分離（`npm run test:e2e:perf`） |
| workers が CPU 数任せ（12並列）で、毎回どれかが落ちる | 4 に制限 |
| ランダム配置とタイマー駆動で稀に取りこぼす | ローカルでも `retries: 1`（繰り返し落ちるものは実際の不具合として検出できる） |

## 計測結果（1280×800、配布ビルドを itch.io と同じサブパス配信で）

| 項目 | 結果 | 基準 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| プレイ中のプレイエリア | **73.7%** | — |
| 常設HUD + 操作バー | **12.1%** | Game Studio: 20-25%以内 ✅ |
| プレイフィールド中央 | オーバーレイなし（目標表示は上端1%の位置） | 中央を空ける ✅ |
| 一時停止 | タイマー停止・さいかい表示 ✅ | — |
| ビューポート4種（1920×1080/1440×900/1280×720/1024×768） | 画面外ボタンなし・pageerror なし ✅ | — |
| コアループ | りんごクリック → 得点10 ✅ | — |

待機中は設定を表示するため常設UIが 29.8% になるが、プレイ中は 12.1% に下がるため基準内と判断した。

## テスト内容

- **ユニットテスト**: 652件 / 59スイート すべて通過
  - `useGameLogicAutoPause` 5件を新規追加（TDD で先に失敗を確認）

> **Stack** (merge bottom-up; each PR targets its parent, retarget to `main` as parents merge — CI re-runs on retarget):
> 1. `refactor/extract-setup-wizard-core` — the `@akasecurity/setup-wizard` extraction
> 2. `feat/codex-plugin` — the Codex CLI plugin
> 3. `feat/claude-ai-source` — the claude-ai source seam
> 4. `feat/browser-extension` — the Chrome extension
> 5. `chore/release-0.10.0` — the version bump
>
> **This PR is #4.**

## What

Adds **`plugins/browser-extension`** — one Chrome (MV3) extension covering ChatGPT (chatgpt.com / chat.openai.com) and Claude.ai web chat, extensible to more providers via a small adapter interface. Plus the **`aka extension`** CLI command that installs its native-messaging bridge.

Architecture (local-first, no server, no port):
- **Detection runs client-side** in the content script: `@akasecurity/detections` depends only on `@akasecurity/schema`, so it bundles cleanly into the browser. Block prevents the send with an inline banner; redact rewrites the composer text before the send proceeds; warn banners and passes through.
- **Persistence goes over Chrome Native Messaging** — the background service worker relays capture events to a Node native host that reuses `createPluginRuntime`/`resolveDataGateway` exactly like the hook scripts, writing to the same `~/.aka/data/aka.db`. No listening port; Chrome will only start the host for an extension id listed in the manifest's `allowed_origins`. That is a wiring constraint rather than a trust boundary — v1 loads unpacked from a public key committed in this repo, so the id it pins is reproducible by anyone who has the repo.
- **Provider adapters** (`providers/chatgpt.ts`, `claude.ts`, `registry.ts`) are the one seam a future provider (Gemini, DeepSeek, …) implements: `match(url)`, `findComposer()`, `extractText()`, `watchSubmit()`.
- **`aka extension install`** writes the native-messaging-host manifest to the OS path (macOS/Linux; Windows via registry) with the settings-file write conventions (tmp-then-rename, `0600`); `aka extension status` reports the wiring. The extension itself is bundled into the CLI package by `prepack` and loaded unpacked.

## Deliberate limits (flagged)

- **Site selectors are unverified against live logged-in sessions.** The adapters target resilient signals (ARIA roles, `contenteditable`, MutationObserver re-bind) rather than class names, and the test suite drives them against fixture DOM built from the adapters' own selector strings — but both sites change markup without notice, so a verification pass against the real pages should precede any wide rollout.
- v1 is **load-unpacked** (a fixed dev keypair pins the extension id so `allowed_origins` never needs per-install updates); Chrome Web Store publishing is an externally-owned follow-up. Edge/Brave share the mechanism (different manifest paths); Firefox is a follow-up.
- CodeQL now sweeps this tree on PRs — worth checking the Security tab for alerts on the new content-script/message-passing code before marking ready for review.

## Tests

Wire framing (length-prefix round-trip, chunk reassembly, oversize rejection), the native host's capture shaping (block → `text:null`, redact → masked rewrite, raw never echoed), the protocol dispatch loop (unknown-type error replies, a throwing handler doesn't kill the host), the background relay (requestId correlation, disconnect resolves all in-flight requests fail-open), the interceptor decision matrix (block/redact/warn/fail-open/re-entrancy), adapter glue on fixture DOM (Enter + button-click watchers, cleanup detaches both), and a manifest-consistency test tying the registry's hostnames to `content_scripts`/`host_permissions` and the native-host name across extension and CLI.

## Verification

Full workspace `turbo run typecheck lint test` green at this tip; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` clean; both dependency-audit gates pass (the new devDeps — esbuild, jsdom, @types/chrome — carry no high/critical advisories; esbuild resolves to the workspace's pinned 0.28.x override).

## Post-draft deep review (internal) — applied

- **Launcher fix (was a blocker):** the native-messaging manifest pointed Chrome at the bare `host.js`, which Chrome cannot spawn on any platform — the bridge would have silently failed open forever. `aka extension install` now writes a per-OS launcher (`#!/bin/sh` exec of the Node runtime on macOS/Linux, a `.cmd` on Windows) and points the manifest at it; under the SEA binary it resolves `node` from PATH or fails loudly.
- `host_permissions` dropped from the manifest — content-script injection needs only `matches`, and the extra grant would have allowed cross-origin reads nothing uses (least privilege, pinned by test).
- The bundled extension's manifest version is stamped from the CLI version at bundle time (chrome://extensions no longer shows a frozen 0.1.0).
- `release-binaries.yml` now runs `bundle:extension` before `package:sea` — without it the first `bin-v0.10.0` tag would have failed on the new packaging guard.
- `aka extension` is documented in the CLI README.

- 이메일 인증 이후 비밀번호, 이름, 회사명, 직무, 약관 동의로 이어지는 회원가입 플로우를 구현했습니다.
- 회원가입 단계별 진입 조건을 공통 가드로 관리하고, 선행 정보가 없으면 실제로 다시 입력해야 하는 단계로 이동하도록 구성했습니다.
- 임시 입력 정보를 Zustand store와 `sessionStorage`에 유지하되, 비밀번호는 브라우저 저장소에 저장하지 않고 메모리에서만 유지하도록 했습니다.
- 이메일과 Google 가입 방식을 구분할 수 있는 인증 상태 구조를 추가했습니다.
  - 현재 PR에는 공통 프로필 단계, 단계 가드, 최종 제출 분기의 기반만 포함합니다.
  - Google Identity Services를 통한 실제 인증 진입은 별도 브랜치에서 진행합니다.
- 이름, 회사명, 비밀번호 및 이메일 폼 검증을 React Hook Form과 Zod 기반으로 통일했습니다.
- 회원가입 입력 폼의 유효성 검사를 다음/제출 버튼 클릭 시점에 수행하도록 변경했습니다.
- 회사명을 필수 입력값으로 검증하고, 회사명 단계를 직접 우회할 수 없도록 단계 가드를 보완했습니다.
- 가입 방식에 따른 최종 회원가입 API 제출 구조를 추가했습니다.
- 공용 Dropdown이 값의 union 타입을 보존하도록 제네릭 API로 개선했습니다.
- 인증 폼 공통 레이아웃과 단계 이동 버튼을 재사용 가능한 컴포넌트로 분리했습니다.
- 단계별 진입 조건, 유효성 검사, 상태 유지, 최종 제출 동작에 대한 테스트와 Storybook 사례를 추가했습니다.
- 리뷰어가 회원가입 구조를 빠르게 확인할 수 있도록 `docs/signup-flow.md`를 추가했습니다.

## 왜 변경했나요?

- [CHA-24: 유효성 검사 시점 변경](https://linear.app/chaesozip/issue/CHA-24/fix-유효성-검사-시점-변경)
- [CHA-18: 회원가입 구현](https://linear.app/chaesozip/issue/CHA-18/feat-회원가입-구현)

이메일 회원가입 과정에서 사용자가 정보를 단계적으로 입력하고, 이전 단계로 이동해도 작성한 내용을 유지할 수 있는 흐름이 필요했습니다.

각 폼에서 개별적으로 관리하던 상태와 검증 로직을 공통 패턴으로 통일해 중복을 줄였습니다. 또한 비밀번호와 Google 가입 토큰 같은 민감한 값을 브라우저 저장소에서 제외하고, 직무와 가입 방식이 안전한 타입 경계를 유지하도록 개선했습니다.
## 확인 사항

### 필수 확인

- [x] `node --run build` 통과
- [x] `node --run lint` 통과
- [x] `node --run test` 통과 또는 관련 테스트 확인
- [x] 관련 이슈를 연결했습니다. 예: `Closes #123`

### 기능 검증

- [x] 변경된 기능을 로컬에서 직접 확인했습니다
- [x] 사용자 플로우가 의도대로 동작하는지 확인했습니다
- [x] API 연동 또는 상태 관리 변경 사항을 확인했습니다
- [x] 에러/로딩/빈 상태 등 예외 케이스를 확인했습니다
- [x] 변경된 동작에 대한 테스트를 추가하거나 업데이트했습니다

### 설정 및 문서

- [x] 회원가입 구조와 주요 설계 결정을 `docs/signup-flow.md`에 문서화했습니다.
- [x] 새로운 의존성이나 설정 변경 사항이 없습니다
- [x] 환경 변수 추가/변경 사항이 없습니다
- [x] 민감한 값, 토큰, 인증 정보가 포함되지 않았습니다

### 해당되는 경우

- [x] 보안 영향을 검토했습니다
- [x] 성능 영향을 검토했습니다
- [x] 기존 동작을 변경하는 내용을 PR 설명에 명확히 작성했습니다
- [ ] 스크린샷 또는 화면 녹화를 첨부했습니다

## 추가 참고

- 약관별 `보기` 버튼의 상세 콘텐츠 연결은 후속 작업으로 구현할 예정입니다.
- Google Identity Services를 통한 실제 Google 인증 진입은 별도 브랜치에서 구현합니다.
- 현재 회원가입 단계는 개별 경로로 구성했습니다. 단일 경로와 쿼리스트링을 사용하는 방식으로의 변경은 후속 논의 대상으로 남겨두었습니다.

author: johnitvn
body:
## Description

A careful reader concluded that changing `dev-cli` would not re-run `core-ui`'s lint, because `core-ui`'s `project.json` declares no dependency on it. **The conclusion is wrong and the observation is fair**: the edge is real, it is already declared, and nothing in any `project.json` points at where.

It lives once, workspace-wide, in `nx.json`:

```json
"lint": {
  "inputs": ["default",
    "{workspaceRoot}/eslint.config.mjs",
    "{workspaceRoot}/shared/tools/eslint-local-rules/**/*",
    "{workspaceRoot}/journey-markers.config.json",
    "{workspaceRoot}/shared/tools/dev-cli/**/*"]
}
```

Two readers reached the same wrong conclusion from the same absence, in the same session. That makes it a gap in the workspace's vocabulary rather than a gap in either reading, and the cost was concrete: it nearly produced a pull request adding a redundant declaration to nine files.

### Measured, not assumed

| change touching only… | projects `nx affected` selects |
| --- | --- |
| `shared/tools/dev-cli/src/check-commit-scope.mjs` | **all 12** — and `test` runs for all 8 projects that have one |
| `shared/libs/core-ui/src/index.ts` | **3** — `core-ui`, `design-system`, `design-system-e2e` |

The second row is the control: `nx affected` is discriminating here, not degenerate, so the first row really is the tooling edge doing its job.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change fixing an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change adding functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature causing existing functionality to change)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Design system / component update
- [ ] Refactor / performance improvement

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated — documentation only, no behaviour to pin
- [x] Manual testing completed
- [ ] UI tested (if applicable) — no user-facing surface
- [ ] Accessibility checked (if applicable) — same

**Test Steps:**

1. Commit a one-line change to a file under `shared/tools/dev-cli/src/`, then run `pnpm nx show projects --affected --base=origin/main --head=HEAD`. Expect all 12 projects.
2. Repeat on a fresh branch with a one-line change to `shared/libs/core-ui/src/index.ts` instead. Expect exactly `core-ui`, `design-system`, `design-system-e2e` — the control proving step 1 is a real edge and not a blanket rebuild.
3. `pnpm nx affected -t test` on the branch from step 1 runs `test` for 8 projects, so the edge reaches more than lint.
4. All 8 doc gates exit 0; `check-commit-scope --commit 46cb2c7` exits 0. `pnpm nx affected -t lint test typecheck build e2e` reports no tasks — `CLAUDE.md` is a workspace-root file in no project, which is expected rather than a skipped gate.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented complex logic (where necessary)
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] Tests pass locally: see Test Steps
- [x] No unrelated code changes included

## AI-Assisted Development

- [x] This PR is AI-assisted (drafted or substantially written by an AI coding agent)

## Additional Notes

### Why the rule went in the root file

It governs every `project.json` in the workspace, including product domains that do not exist yet. `shared/CLAUDE.md` only loads when work happens inside that tree, so a reader editing a future domain's `project.json` would never receive it. Root is the tier whose delivery mechanism reaches the paths the rule binds.

It **extends the existing `pnpm nx` bullet** rather than adding a section — that bullet already named `targetDefaults` as a source of truth; it now says what that means for the case people actually hit.

### No `practice-index.json` card

The index's `$admission` asks whether auto-loading can deliver the rule. Root `CLAUDE.md` is always in context, so it can. A rule that applies to everything adds no routing information and stays out.

### Should `implicitDependencies: ["dev-cli"]` be added to the nine projects that lack it? No.

- It is **already declared**, once. Nine copies of one workspace fact is precisely the unsynced duplicate Rule 14 names — *"a value copied across ≥2 files was never a valid hardcode, it was an unsynced config that skipped rung 2."*
- `implicitDependencies` is also the **coarser instrument**. It creates a project-level graph edge, which participates in `dependsOn: ["^build"]` chains on `build` and `typecheck`. The dependency being modelled is narrower than that: lint runs a CLI.

### Residue, named rather than fixed

`design-system-e2e` and `doctrine-site-e2e` **do** list `dev-cli` in `implicitDependencies`, and for affectedness it is redundant — removing it from `design-system-e2e` drops the graph edge (leaving `design-system` and `core-ui`) and the project is *still* selected by a `dev-cli`-only change, because `targetDefaults.lint.inputs` already reaches it. Verified directly on a throwaway branch.

They are left in place deliberately. Both projects' `e2e` target really does invoke `dev-cli run-e2e`, and that dependence is currently carried by **lint's** inputs rather than declared for `e2e` — so deleting the redundant entries would couple e2e correctness to a line about lint. The honest fix is `targetDefaults.e2e.inputs`, which changes task caching and belongs to its own change rather than to a documentation pass. Recorded here so the next reader inherits the finding instead of rediscovering it.

> **Stack** (merge bottom-up; each PR targets its parent, retarget to `main` as parents merge — CI re-runs on retarget):
> 1. `refactor/extract-setup-wizard-core` — the `@akasecurity/setup-wizard` extraction
> 2. `feat/codex-plugin` — the Codex CLI plugin
> 3. `feat/claude-ai-source` — the claude-ai source seam
> 4. `feat/browser-extension` — the Chrome extension
> 5. `chore/release-0.10.0` — the version bump
>
> **This PR is #5.**

## What

`chore(release): 0.10.0` — the minor bump for this stack, kept out of the feature PRs so each of them stays reviewable against main's 0.9.3 line.

Five files move together (the shared version line per CLAUDE.md's release rules):

- `cli/package.json` → 0.10.0
- `plugins/claude-code/package.json` + `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` → 0.10.0
- `plugins/codex/package.json` + `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` → 0.10.0

Minor (not patch) because the stack adds new surface: the Codex CLI plugin, the claude-ai source seam, the browser extension + `aka extension` command, and the `@akasecurity/setup-wizard` extraction bundled into all three artifacts.

## Guardrails

Both plugins carry a version-lockstep test (plugin manifest === package.json), and the codex suite adds a three-way shared-line assertion (cli === claude-code plugin === codex plugin), so a partial bump now fails CI instead of publishing mismatched artifacts. `@akasecurity/plugin-browser-extension` stays private/unpublished and is deliberately not on the shared line.

## Verification

Full workspace `turbo run typecheck lint test` green at this tip; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` clean; both dependency-audit gates (workspace + cli artifact) pass.

cudnn indexer 移除了对 THD 格式的各种限制（包括必须被 ratio 整除、不支持单 token 文本、不支持 CP 等），目前 THD 已经完全可用，32K 下 cudnn_indexer_fwd 的用时仅为原来 dense 实现的 40%，端到端提升待测试


body:
NVD CPE data often uses canonical dotted numeric versions, such as 153.0.0, while Nix package versions may use shorter forms such as 153.0. Treat pure dotted numeric versions as equivalent after dropping trailing zero components for exact CPE matches and version ranges.

Keep exact CPE matches strict for non-numeric versions. Preserve the existing Nix comparator fallback for non-numeric range checks, and use comparator results for inclusive range bounds so versions that compare equal satisfy inclusive CPE bounds.

Cache dotted numeric parsing because CPE version matching runs in the scanner inner loop.

Add regression coverage for Firefox 153.0 against a versionEndExcluding 153.0.0 range and exact 153.0.0 CPEs.

body:
## Vì sao cần PR này

PR #649 (nới `maxReplicas`) **đã chạy đủ 8 stage và không nâng được trần**:

| Users | RPS baseline | RPS tuned | Verdict b/t |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 531,1 | 525,5 | PASS/PASS ← trần cả hai arm |
| 1400 | 601,1 | 602,0 | FAIL/FAIL |

Nới trần replica là **cần nhưng không đủ** — nút thắt không nằm ở số replica.

## Nút thắt thật: `email` — queue depth, không phải CPU

Đo exact-window, stage 1400 user, node-set cố định 9 node (`3d67a92aaa5e88a1`):

| Điểm đo | p95 |
|---|---|
| span CLIENT `POST` checkout → email | **15000 ms** (= route timeout Envoy) |
| span SERVER email | **391 ms** |

14,6 giây chênh lệch là **xếp hàng**, không phải xử lý — đúng loại bão hoà directive #19 gọi tên (*"không phải chậm - mà cạn: connection/queue depth"*).

Vì sao nó kéo sập checkout: `checkout` gọi `sendOrderConfirmation` **đồng bộ** (`src/checkout/main.go:473`), không đặt deadline riêng → hàng đợi email ăn trọn budget 15s → **504**. Stage vỡ: **3.432/5.431 đơn hỏng = 82% toàn bộ lỗi client**.

Vì sao 1 replica không đủ: Ruby/Sinatra trên Puma (MRI có GIL), limit CPU **100m = 0,1 core**, tải 14,7 rps × 391 ms ≈ 5,8 request đồng thời.

## Nguồn lỗi browse: deadline 500ms, không retry

Log frontend @1400: `4 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: Deadline exceeded after 0.500s`.
`product-catalog` p95 server-side chỉ **6,9 ms** — deadline không quá thấp so với trung vị, nó quá sát **đuôi**. Không có retry nên timeout thành lỗi cứng: **311 × HTTP 500** (`/api/products/[id]`) + **431 × HTTP 503** (`/api/product-reviews/[id]`) = 742 lỗi, đúng phần kéo browse xuống 99,06%.

## Thay đổi (config-only — không rebuild image, không thêm node)

| Service | Thay đổi | Căn cứ đo |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | HPA 2..8 @60% (mới); req 25m→75m; limit 100m→**600m** | nút thắt, 82% lỗi |
| `frontend` | `PRODUCT_CATALOG_DEADLINE_MS`, `PRODUCT_REVIEWS_DEADLINE_MS` 500→**1200** | 742 lỗi browse |
| `accounting` | req 50m→150m; limit 200m→**600m** | throttle **86,1%** |
| `recommendation` | req 100m→150m; limit 500m→700m | throttle 18,1% |

MIGraphX cannot run the YOLOv3 model because the model contains loop subgraphs. This PR resolves the parsing and compiling issues associated with this subgraph.

<!-- Explain the changes along with any relevant GitHub links. -->
1,  Handle duplicate loop subgraphs during parsing

author: mpretty-cyro
body:
The community specs shared a fixed set of rooms, so two runs against the same SOGS - CI and a laptop, or two CI jobs - joined, posted, pinned and banned in the same place, and a test had to leave its rooms usable for the next one.

A spec now declares `communityRooms: <n>` and is given rooms created for it alone, deleted in its teardown. Room tokens carry a per-run id so concurrent runs cannot delete each other's rooms, only `qa-`-prefixed rooms are ever removed, and a gc sweep at the start of each run collects what an interrupted run left behind.

`communities` resolves per test rather than at module load. Reading it without declaring `communityRooms` throws: returning a shared room silently is the behaviour this replaces, and it would fail somewhere unrelated to the cause.

Rooms are managed through Sesh-Net-Docker's `sogs/room.sh`, or over HTTP when SOGS_ROOM_API and SOGS_ROOM_API_TOKEN are set - for hosts that can reach the SOGS container but cannot `docker exec` into it. PySOGS has no room-creation endpoint, so one of the two is required.

Whether rooms can be created is settled once at startup. If neither transport works the run falls back to the shared rooms with a warning rather than failing, since that configuration still exercises everything - it just cannot isolate concurrent runs. Without COMMUNITY_LINK the suite uses the remote communities exactly as before, so this is inert anywhere a local SOGS isn't configured.
